- entire-engineering:design:design-implementation-reviewer: Use this agent when you need to verify that a UI implementation matches its Figma design specifications. This agent should be called after code has been written to implement a design, particularly after HTML/CSS/React components have been created or modified. The agent will visually compare the live implementation against the Figma design and provide detailed feedback on discrepancies.

Examples:
- <example>
  Context: The user has just implemented a new component based on a Figma design.
  user: "I've finished implementing the hero section based on the Figma design"
  assistant: "I'll review how well your implementation matches the Figma design."
  <commentary>
  Since UI implementation has been completed, use the design-implementation-reviewer agent to compare the live version with Figma.
  </commentary>
  </example>
- <example>

  user: "Update the button styles to match the new design system"
  assistant: "I've updated the button styles. Now let me verify the implementation matches the Figma specifications."
  <commentary>

  </commentary>
  </example> (Tools: All tools)

Perfect when colors feel wrong, layouts aren't balanced, or the overall aesthetic needs work that single changes can't achieve. <example>Context: User asks to change button color but result still looks off. user: "Change the button to blue" assistant: [makes change, takes screenshot] "The button is now blue, but I notice the overall color balance still feels off. Would you like me to use the design-iterator agent with 5 iterations to systematically improve the color harmony and visual balance?" <commentary>PROACTIVE USE: After a simple change doesn't fully resolve the design issue, suggest the design-iterator to do deeper work.</commentary></example> <example>Context: User's design request leads to something that doesn't look right. user: "Make the hero section more modern" assistant: [makes initial changes] "I've added some modern elements, but the result isn't quite coming together. This looks like it needs iterative refinement. ## claude.ai Linear
When passing string values to tools, send the content directly without escape sequences. For example, use real newlines in markdown content rather than literal backslash-n (\n) characters.

## plugin:datadog:mcp
This is an MCP server for Datadog (a software observability platform). Consult Datadog docs if you're unsure about how something works in the platform. Docs for this MCP server can be found at https://docs.datadoghq.com/bits_ai/mcp_server/setup/ This server ships skill guides containing domain-specific guidance, workflows, and best practices that are not visible in tool names or schemas. Before invoking other tools, always perform skill discovery by running both paths in parallel: a direct load with `load_datadog_skill` using a general domain name (e.g. skill_name='datadog/traces'), and a call to `list_datadog_skills` with a fuzzy `query` based on topic keywords — load any clearly matching result from the listing along with the related skills it points to. The exception is a follow-up call in a domain whose skill you have already loaded or confirmed absent this session. If nothing clearly fits, do not load a skill — proceed with the tool descriptions. When the user asks to visualize, chart, or graph data — or when loading a data domain skill (e.g. datadog/traces, datadog/logs, datadog/metrics) — also load datadog/visualizations. Investigation results often benefit from charts.

Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").

TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

32	func (a *PiAgent) HookNames() []string {

41	// GetSupportedHooks maps Pi's native events to normalised lifecycle types.
42	//
43	//   - session_start       → SessionStart
44	//   - before_agent_start  → TurnStart
45	//   - agent_end           → TurnEnd
46	//   - session_shutdown    → (cleanup-only, no lifecycle event — see ParseHookEvent)
47	func (a *PiAgent) GetSupportedHooks() []agent.HookType {
48		return []agent.HookType{
49			agent.HookSessionStart,
50			agent.HookUserPromptSubmit,
51			agent.HookStop,
52		}
53	}

55	// Compile-time assertion that Pi can inject context into the model.

58	// InjectionEvent reports that Pi injects model context at TurnStart
59	// (before_agent_start) — the only Pi event where the embedded extension can
60	// return a message that Pi stores in the session and sends to the LLM.
61	func (a *PiAgent) InjectionEvent() agent.EventType { return agent.TurnStart }
62	
63	// RenderContextInjection emits a {"inject_context":"..."} envelope on stdout.
64	// The embedded extension (entire_extension.ts) reads it from the
65	// before_agent_start hook's stdout and returns it to Pi as a hidden persistent
66	// message. An empty Text renders nothing.
67	func (a *PiAgent) RenderContextInjection(inj agent.ContextInjection) ([]byte, error) {
68		if strings.TrimSpace(inj.Text) == "" {
69			return nil, nil
70		}
71		b, err := json.Marshal(struct {
72			InjectContext string `json:"inject_context"`
73		}{InjectContext: inj.Text})
74		if err != nil {
75			return nil, fmt.Errorf("marshal pi context injection: %w", err)
76		}
77		return append(b, '\n'), nil
78	}

97	// piSkillEvents converts the Pi extension's live skill-invocation reports into
98	// agent.SkillEvents. This is Pi's only skill-capture path. PiAgent intentionally
99	// does NOT implement agent.SkillEventExtractor: a transcript extractor would
100	// double-count these live events at condensation (see
101	// TestPiAgent_UsesLiveSkillCaptureNotTranscriptExtraction).
102	func piSkillEvents(in []piSkillEventInput) []agent.SkillEvent {
103		if len(in) == 0 {
104			return nil
105		}
106		out := make([]agent.SkillEvent, 0, len(in))
107		for i, ev := range in {
108			skillName := strings.TrimSpace(ev.SkillName)
109			if skillName == "" {
110				continue
111			}
112			invocation := strings.TrimSpace(ev.Invocation)
113			if invocation == "" {
114				invocation = "/skill:" + skillName
115			}
116			id := ""
117			if ev.Timestamp != "" {
118				id = fmt.Sprintf("pi-skill-%s-%s-%d", skillName, ev.Timestamp, i)
119			}
120			out = append(out, agent.SkillEvent{
121				ID:        id,
122				EventType: agent.SkillEventTypePromptInvocation,
123				Skill: agent.SkillEventSkill{
124					Name: skillName,
125				},
126				Source: agent.SkillEventSource{
127					Agent:      string(agent.AgentNamePi),
128					Signal:     agent.SkillSignalPiInputSlashCommand,
129					Confidence: agent.SkillConfidenceExplicit,
130				},
131				Timestamp: ev.Timestamp,
132				Native: map[string]string{
133					"command": invocation,
134				},
135				Collapse: agent.SkillEventCollapse{
136					Target:           agent.SkillCollapseTargetUserMessage,
137					Label:            invocation,
138					DefaultCollapsed: true,
139				},
140			})
141		}
142		return out
143	}

147	func (a *PiAgent) ParseHookEvent(ctx context.Context, hookName string, stdin io.Reader) (*agent.Event, error) {
148		// Stream one JSON value rather than io.ReadAll so the hook never blocks
149		// waiting for stdin EOF that some agents don't send on Windows (issue #1398).
150		parsed, err := agent.ReadAndParseHookInput[piHookPayload](stdin)

153		}
154		payload := *parsed

156		sessionID := payload.SessionID

159		}
160	
161		now := time.Now()
162	
163		switch hookName {
164		case HookNameSessionStart:
165			cacheSessionID(ctx, sessionID)
166			return &agent.Event{
167				Type:      agent.SessionStart,
168				SessionID: sessionID,
169				Timestamp: now,
170			}, nil
171	
172		case HookNameBeforeAgentStart:
173			// Pi emits before_agent_start with a fully-populated session ID, but
174			// we cache it anyway to support the agent_end fallback below.
175			if sessionID == "" {
176				sessionID = readCachedSessionID(ctx)
177			} else {
178				cacheSessionID(ctx, sessionID)
179			}
180			// Provide the live Pi session file as SessionRef so state.TranscriptPath
181			// is populated before any mid-turn commits. Without this, the
182			// post-commit hook cannot condense when no shadow branch exists yet.
183			return &agent.Event{
184				Type:        agent.TurnStart,
185				SessionID:   sessionID,
186				SessionRef:  payload.SessionFile,
187				Prompt:      payload.Prompt,
188				Timestamp:   now,
189				SkillEvents: piSkillEvents(payload.SkillEvents),
190			}, nil
191	
192		case HookNameAgentEnd:

194				sessionID = readCachedSessionID(ctx)

docs/KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md:48:When multiple sessions are ACTIVE in the same directory and one session's agent (or subagent) makes a commit, **all** ACTIVE sessions are condensed — including sessions that didn't contribute to the commit. This can produce checkpoint entries with minimal content (e.g., just the initial prompt) linked to a commit the session didn't work on.
docs/KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md:50:**Why:** PostCommit sets `hasNew=true` for all ACTIVE sessions. We cannot re-validate via transcript analysis because subagent file modifications live in a separate transcript from the main agent's. Attempting to re-validate causes subagent commits to skip condensation entirely (data loss), which is worse than a spurious empty checkpoint.
docs/security-and-privacy.md:11:Entire also creates temporary local branches (e.g., `entire/<short-hash>`) as working storage during a session. Metadata written to these shadow branches — transcripts, prompts, incremental checkpoint data, subagent transcripts — goes through the same redaction pipeline as `entire/checkpoints/v1`. **Code-file snapshots, however, are written as raw blobs of your working tree without redaction**, so any hardcoded secrets in your source code would appear unredacted on the shadow branch. Gitignored files (e.g., `.env`) are filtered out of these snapshots as a partial defense. Shadow branches are **not** pushed by Entire; do not push them manually, because unredacted source content would be visible on the remote. They are cleaned up when session data is condensed into `entire/checkpoints/v1` at commit time.

docs/KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md:48:When multiple sessions are ACTIVE in the same directory and one session's agent (or subagent) makes a commit, **all** ACTIVE sessions are condensed — including sessions that didn't contribute to the commit. This can produce checkpoint entries with minimal content (e.g., just the initial prompt) linked to a commit the session didn't work on.
docs/KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md:50:**Why:** PostCommit sets `hasNew=true` for all ACTIVE sessions. We cannot re-validate via transcript analysis because subagent file modifications live in a separate transcript from the main agent's. Attempting to re-validate causes subagent commits to skip condensation entirely (data loss), which is worse than a spurious empty checkpoint.
docs/security-and-privacy.md:11:Entire also creates temporary local branches (e.g., `entire/<short-hash>`) as working storage during a session. Metadata written to these shadow branches — transcripts, prompts, incremental checkpoint data, subagent transcripts — goes through the same redaction pipeline as `entire/checkpoints/v1`. **Code-file snapshots, however, are written as raw blobs of your working tree without redaction**, so any hardcoded secrets in your source code would appear unredacted on the shadow branch. Gitignored files (e.g., `.env`) are filtered out of these snapshots as a partial defense. Shadow branches are **not** pushed by Entire; do not push them manually, because unredacted source content would be visible on the remote. They are cleaned up when session data is condensed into `entire/checkpoints/v1` at commit time.

56	// Checkpoints are stored at sharded paths: <id[:2]>/<id[2:]>/

59	//   - For incremental checkpoints: checkpoints/NNN-<tool-use-id>.json
60	//   - For final checkpoints: checkpoint.json and agent-<agent-id>.jsonl
61	func (s *GitStore) writeSession(ctx context.Context, opts WriteOptions) error {

63		// canceled ctx means stop doing work, and creating a checkpoint is the most
64		// expensive write there is. Nothing below here observes cancellation

66		// without this a bulk writer that ignores cancellation keeps minting
67		// checkpoints after Ctrl-C.

77		}

80		}
81		if err := validation.ValidateAgentID(opts.AgentID); err != nil {
82			return fmt.Errorf("invalid checkpoint options: %w", err)
83		}

85		// Ensure sessions branch exists
86		if err := s.ensureSessionsBranch(ctx); err != nil {

88		}
89	
90		// Get branch ref and root tree hash (O(1), no flatten)
91		parentHash, rootTreeHash, err := s.getSessionsBranchRef()
92		if err != nil {
93			return err
94		}
95	
96		// Build the new checkpoint subtree from its current state on the v1 branch,
97		// then splice it back at the shard path. basePath keeps the v1 sharded layout
98		// so stored session-file pointers stay /<shard>/<id>/<n>/... as before.
99		existing, err := s.subtreeObjAt(rootTreeHash, opts.CheckpointID.Path())
100		if err != nil {
101			return err
102		}
103		checkpointSubtree, taskMetadataPath, err := s.applySessionWrite(ctx, opts, existing, opts.CheckpointID.Path()+"/")
104		if err != nil {
105			return err
106		}
107	
108		newTreeHash, err := s.spliceCheckpointSubtree(rootTreeHash, opts.CheckpointID, checkpointSubtree)
109		if err != nil {
110			return err
111		}
112		newTreeHash, err = s.maybeMergeVercelConfig(ctx, newTreeHash)
113		if err != nil {
114			return err
115		}
116	
117		commitMsg := s.buildCommitMessage(opts, taskMetadataPath)
118		newCommitHash, err := CreateCommit(ctx, s.repo, newTreeHash, parentHash, commitMsg, opts.AuthorName, opts.AuthorEmail)
119		if err != nil {
120			return err
121		}
122	
123		return s.setPrimaryRef(newCommitHash)
124	}

- Use read-modify-write on entire `hooks.json` file
- Preserve unknown keys in the `hooks` object (future event types)
- The `hooks.json` is separate from `config.toml` — safe to create/modify independently

## CLI Flags

- Non-interactive prompt: `codex exec "<prompt>"` or `codex exec --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox "<prompt>"`
- Interactive mode: `codex` or `codex "<prompt>"` (starts TUI)
- Resume session: `codex resume <session-id>` or `codex resume --last`
- Model override: `-m <model>` or `--model <model>`
- Full-auto mode: `codex exec --full-auto "<prompt>"` (workspace-write sandbox + auto-approve)
- JSONL output: `codex exec --json "<prompt>"` (events to stdout)
- Relevant env vars: `CODEX_HOME` (config dir override), `OPENAI_API_KEY` (API auth)

## Gaps & Limitations

- **Hooks require feature flag:** The `codex_hooks` feature is `default_enabled: false` (stage: UnderDevelopment). It must be enabled via `--enable codex_hooks` CLI flag, or `features.codex_hooks = true` in `config.toml`, or `-c features.codex_hooks=true`. Without this, hooks.json is ignored entirely.
- **No SessionEnd hook:** Codex does not fire a hook when a session is completely terminated. The `Stop` hook fires at end-of-turn, not end-of-session. This is similar to some other agents — the framework handles this gracefully.
- **PreToolUse is shell-only:** Currently only fires for `Bash` tool (direct shell execution). MCP tools, stdin streaming, and other tool types are not yet hooked. PostToolUse is in review.
- **Transcript may be null:** In `--ephemeral` mode, `transcript_path` is null. The integration should handle this gracefully.
- **No subagent hooks:** No PreTask/PostTask equivalent for subagent spawning.
- **Hook response protocol differs from Claude Code:** Codex uses `systemMessage` (same field name) but also supports `hookSpecificOutput` with `additionalContext` for injecting context into the model. For Entire's purposes, `systemMessage` is sufficient.

## Captured Payloads

- JSON schemas at `codex-rs/hooks/schema/generated/` in the Codex repository
- Hook config structure at `codex-rs/hooks/src/engine/config.rs` in the Codex repository

## Review integration (`entire review`)

Codex review runs via `codex exec --skip-git-repo-check --json [-m <model>] [-c model_reasoning_effort=<level>] -` (prompt on stdin). **`codex exec` fires no lifecycle hooks**, which shapes the whole integration (see CLAUDE.md → `entire review` → "Codex specifics"):

- **Skills are passed verbatim, not paraphrased.** Codex injects its installed-skill catalog into every exec session and loads the matching `SKILL.md`; configured skills use codex's `$name` / `$plugin:name` form (`DiscoverReviewSkills` in `discovery.go`). Native `codex exec review` is not used — it rejects a prompt under a scope flag and can't carry Entire's scope/per-run/checkpoint context.
- **Live tokens come from the rollout file, not stdout.** `codex exec --json` carries `usage` only on the terminal `turn.completed`, and a review is a single turn. `review_tokens.go` resolves the rollout transcript by `thread_id` (from the `thread.started` envelope), tails it (the same `~/.codex/.../rollout-*-<thread-id>.jsonl` documented under Transcript above), and emits cumulative `Tokens` per `token_count` event — the source codex's interactive UI reads.
- **No tagged review session.** Because no hook fires, codex's session is never tagged `KindAgentReview`. The fix manifest therefore sources codex from its **live run output** (`run.Buffer`), and `entire review fix` skill verification is advisory for codex (loose description match), not a hard block.

Enable Entire with session tracking for your AI agent workflows.

If Entire is not yet configured, this runs the full configuration flow.
If Entire is already configured but disabled, this re-enables it.

If the current directory is not a git repository, Entire can initialize one
for you and (optionally) create a matching GitHub repository via the gh CLI.

Usage:
  entire enable [flags]

Flags:
      --absolute-git-hook-path               Embed full binary path in git hooks (for GUI git clients that don't source shell profiles)
      --agent string                         Agent to set up hooks for (e.g., claude-code, codex, copilot-cli, cursor, factoryai-droid, gemini, opencode, pi; external agents on $PATH are also available). Enables non-interactive mode.
      --agent-help-skill entire agent-help   Install the stable Entire agent-help skill (points agents at entire agent-help) for selected agent(s)
      --checkpoint-backend string            Checkpoint storage backend: refs (one git ref per checkpoint; recommended) or branch (shared entire/checkpoints/v1 branch)
      --checkpoint-remote string             Checkpoint remote in provider:owner/repo format (e.g., github:org/checkpoints-repo)
  -f, --force                                Force reinstall hooks (removes existing Entire hooks first)
  -h, --help                                 help for enable
      --import-history                       During first-time setup, import the selected agents' existing session history (last 30 days) without prompting
      --init-repo                            If not a git repo, initialize one non-interactively
      --initial-commit-message string        Commit message for the initial commit when bootstrapping a new repo
      --local                                Write settings to .entire/settings.local.json instead of .entire/settings.json
      --no-github                            Initialize local git repo only; skip creating a GitHub remote
      --no-init-repo                         If not a git repo, exit instead of prompting to initialize one
      --project                              Write settings to .entire/settings.json even if it already exists
      --push                                 When bootstrapping a new repo, push the initial commit to the created GitHub remote (implies creating the remote; without it the repo is created but not pushed)
      --repo-name string                     GitHub repository name for the new repo (used when bootstrapping)
      --repo-owner string                    GitHub user or organization login for the new repo
      --repo-visibility string               GitHub repository visibility: public, private, or internal
      --search-skill                         Install the optional Entire search skill for selected agent(s)
      --skip-initial-commit                  Don't create the initial commit when bootstrapping a new repo
      --skip-push-sessions                   Disable automatic pushing of session logs on git push
      --telemetry                            Enable anonymous usage analytics (default true)
  -y, --yes                                  Accept all defaults without prompting (in a non-repo directory: init git, create private GitHub repo, commit, and push; then enable all agents and accept telemetry). Does not import existing agent history — see --import-history

input.content:
---
name: subagent-tracking-gaps
description: Verified state of subagent tracking in the CLI (2026-08-10) — CC transcript-path bug, no subagent data in committed checkpoints, codex now has subagent hooks, pi subagents hijack the parent session
metadata:
  type: project
---

Investigated 2026-08-10 with hook-level probes against the real binary plus upstream
sources at `/Users/soph/Work/entire/research/codex` and `/Users/soph/Work/entire/research/pi-mono`.

**Claude Code (2.1.221) subagent transcript path is wrong.** `handleLifecycleSubagentEnd`
resolves `AgentTranscriptPath(filepath.Dir(SessionRef), agentID)` → `<slug>/agent-<id>.jsonl`,
but CC now stores it at `<slug>/<session-id>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl` (plus a
`agent-<id>.meta.json` carrying `agentType`, `description`, `toolUseId`, `spawnDepth`).
So `SubagentTranscriptPath` is always empty in production — confirmed: every real
`"subagent completed"` log line across three repos lacks the `subagent_transcript` attr,
and shadow `tasks/<id>/` holds only `checkpoint.json`, no subagent transcript. The TurnEnd
extractor (`lifecycle.go` ~line 848) uses the *correct* `<dir>/<sessionID>/subagents` path,
which masks the bug because files get picked up at Stop.

**Committed checkpoints carry zero subagent data.** Condensation (`extractSessionData`)
reads only `full.jsonl` + `prompt.txt` from the shadow tree, so `tasks/<tool-use-id>/`
is dropped. 0 of 80 primary checkpoint refs in the `cli` repo contain `tasks/`; only a
legacy `v2/full` bundle does. `subagent_tokens` is null in every sampled committed
checkpoint (the two `//TODO: why do we not use here subagents dir?` in
`manual_commit_condensation.go` are why). `TaskStepContext` has no `TokenUsage` field at
all, and the persistent store's `IsTask`/`tasks/` write path is never invoked in production.

**Codex 0.147 DOES have subagent hooks now** — `subagent-start`/`subagent-stop` schemas in
`codex-rs/hooks/schema/generated/`; stop payload includes `agent_id`, `agent_type`,
`agent_transcript_path`, `turn_id`. `hooks` and `multi_agent` are both `stable/true`.
`cmd/entire/cli/agent/codex/AGENT.md` claiming "No subagent hooks" and "hooks require
feature flag" is stale.

**Pi subagents hijack the parent session.** Pi has no subagent events; subagents come from
the `subagent/` example extension, which spawns `pi --mode json -p --no-session` with
`cwd` = project dir. That child auto-discovers project-local `.pi/extensions/entire/index.ts`
and fires Entire's hooks. With `--no-session` there is no `session_file`, so pi's
`readCachedSessionID` (a single per-repo file, not per-process) returns the *parent's* ID.
Probed effect: child `session_start` errors "no session_id"; child `before_agent_start`
succeeds and overwrites the parent's `last_prompt` with the subagent's internal task text
and starts a new `turn_id`; child `agent_end` fails "transcript file not specified".

**Test coverage gaps:** the Vogon/roger-roger canary fires no subagent hooks at all
(`e2e/vogon/main.go` has no pre-task/post-task), so `TestSubagentCommitFlow` passes without
exercising the path; the real-agent version asserts nothing subagent-specific. Only
`cmd/entire/cli/integration_test/subagent_*.go` covers it, via simulated hooks against the

content.text:
## What I tested

Real-agent E2E didn't work out here, so I probed the production hook entrypoints directly (temp repos, real `entire` binary, real upstream payload shapes) and cross-checked against your own production logs and checkpoints.

| Probe | Result |
|---|---|
| Vogon canary `TestSubagentCommitFlow` | Passes — but **fires no subagent hooks at all**; `e2e/vogon/main.go` has no pre-task/post-task. Zero real coverage. |
| Claude Code real E2E | **Blocked locally**: `cleanConfigDir` hands the agent a blank `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, so it reports "Not logged in". Only works in CI (which links `~/.claude/.claude.json`). |
| Claude Code hook-level probe | pre-task → post-task → stop → commit all fire correctly; task checkpoint lands on the shadow branch and shows as `[Task] Completed 'dev' agent: …` in `checkpoint list`. |
| Codex real E2E | You declined the run — not executed. |
| Codex hooks | No subagent verbs registered (`session-start`, `user-prompt-submit`, `stop`, `pre-tool-use`, `post-tool-use` only). |
| Pi nested-subagent probe | Parent session gets hijacked (details below). |

## Four confirmed defects

**1. Claude Code's subagent transcript is never captured.** `handleLifecycleSubagentEnd` (`cmd/entire/cli/lifecycle.go:1152`) looks for `<slug>/agent-<id>.jsonl`. CC 2.1.221 actually writes `<slug>/<session-id>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl`. Production proof: every `"subagent completed"` line in `cli/`, `cli_experiments/` and `cli_experiments_2/` logs has `agent_id` but no `subagent_transcript` attr — it only logs when the path resolves. Consequence: task checkpoints store no subagent transcript, and file extraction silently falls back to scanning the *main* transcript, where the subagent's edits don't appear. The TurnEnd extractor at `lifecycle.go:848` uses the correct path, which is why files still get picked up at Stop — that masks it.

Bonus: upstream now also writes `agent-<id>.meta.json` with `agentType`, `description`, `toolUseId`, `spawnDepth` — ready-made attribution, including nesting depth, which Entire doesn't model.

**2. Committed checkpoints carry no subagent data.** `extractSessionData` reads only `full.jsonl` + `prompt.txt` from the shadow tree, so `tasks/<tool-use-id>/` is dropped at condensation. **0 of 80** primary checkpoint refs in your `cli` repo contain `tasks/` (the 69 hits I found are in a legacy `v2/full` bundle). `subagent_tokens` is `null` in all 30 checkpoints I sampled — including sessions that ran dozens of subagents. The two `//TODO: why do we not use here subagents dir?` in `manual_commit_condensation.go` are exactly this. `TaskStepContext` has no `TokenUsage` field, and the persistent store's `IsTask`/`tasks/` layout is never written in production.

**3. Codex has subagent hooks now and we ignore them.** `codex-rs/hooks/schema/generated/` defines `subagent-start`/`subagent-stop`; the stop payload carries `agent_id`, `agent_type`, **`agent_transcript_path`**, `turn_id`. Both `hooks` and `multi_agent` are `stable/true` in 0.147. `codex/AGENT.md` still says "No subagent hooks" and "hooks require feature flag" — both stale.

**4. Pi subagents corrupt the parent session.** Pi has no subagent events; subagents come from the `subagent/` example extension, which spawns `pi --mode json -p --no-session` with `cwd` = the project. That child auto-discovers project-local `.pi/extensions/entire/index.ts` and fires our hooks. With no session file, pi's `readCachedSessionID` — one per-repo file, not per-process — returns the *parent's* ID. Probed: child `session_start` errors `no session_id`; child `before_agent_start` **succeeds and overwrites the parent's `last_prompt`** with the subagent's internal `Task: …` text and starts a fresh `turn_id`; child `agent_end` fails `transcript file not specified`. So the checkpoint title becomes the last subagent's internal prompt and turn windows reset mid-turn.

## What needs doing

**Fix the bugs (small, high value)**
1. Resolve the CC subagent transcript at `<dir>/<session-id>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl`, keeping the old path as fallback. Read `meta.json` for `agentType`/`description`/`spawnDepth` instead of only parsing `tool_input`.
2. Guard pi against nested invocations (mark the child via env when spawning is detectable, or refuse a turn whose session ID came from cache with no session file) so it can't clobber the parent's prompt/turn.
3. Pass the subagents dir at the two condensation TODOs, or explicitly document why not — right now `subagent_tokens` never survives a commit.

**Decide the data model (the actual "proper tracking" question)**
4. Should subagent work be visible *after* commit? If yes: carry `tasks/<tool-use-id>/` into the committed tree (the persistent store already has the layout), enrich the task record — today it's just `session_id`/`tool_use_id`/`checkpoint_uuid`/`agent_id`, with no subagent type, description, files, tokens, or timings — and surface it (`explain`, `status`, `session tokens` already has a Subagents row it can rarely populate). If no, say so in the docs and stop building toward it.
5. Replace the cumulative-`SubagentTokens`-with-delta-rescoping-in-three-places contract with a per-subagent record; it's the fragile core of the token story.

**Codex + Pi integration**
6. Wire codex `subagent-start`/`subagent-stop` → `SubagentStart`/`SubagentEnd` (its `agent_transcript_path` makes this the cleanest integration of the three), plus a `SubagentAwareExtractor` over subagent rollouts. Refresh `AGENT.md`.
7. For pi, decide whether extension-provided subagents are in scope at all; if yes it needs a `tool_call`-based bridge in `entire_extension.ts`, since there's no native event.

**Coverage**
8. Teach Vogon to fire pre-task/post-task so the canary actually exercises the path in CI.
9. Make `TestSubagentCommitFlow` assert something subagent-specific (task checkpoint exists, subagent transcript stored, subagent tokens non-nil).
10. Add a subagent section to `docs/architecture/agent-integration-checklist.md` — it currently says nothing, so every new agent integration skips this.

Probe repos are kept under `…/scratchpad/probe-cc`, `probe-cc2`, `probe-pi` if you want to replay any of it. Want me to run the Codex E2E (it was declined) or start on the two path bugs?

input.description: Read doc section on subagent transcripts

content.content:
Fires after a subagent finishes its work. Creates the final checkpoint for the subagent's task.

**What it does:**

1.  **Parse Input**: Extracts `tool_use_id`, `agent_id` (from `tool_response.agentId`), `session_id`, `transcript_path`, and `tool_input`.

2.  **Locate Subagent Transcript**:

    - Constructs path: `<transcript_dir>/agent-<agent_id>.jsonl`.
    - If the subagent transcript exists, uses it for file extraction; otherwise falls back to main transcript.

3.  **Extract Modified Files**: Parses the transcript (subagent or main) to find Write/Edit tool invocations.

4.  **Compute New Files**:

    - Loads pre-task state from `.entire/tmp/pre-task-<tool-use-id>.json`.
    - Compares current untracked files against the pre-task snapshot.
    - Files that are now untracked but weren't before = files created by the subagent.

5.  **Find Checkpoint UUID**: Scans the main transcript for any checkpoint UUID associated with this `tool_use_id` (used for rewind linking).

6.  **Save Final Checkpoint**:

    - Builds `TaskCheckpointContext` with all file changes, transcript paths, subagent info, and checkpoint UUID.
    - Calls `strategy.SaveTaskCheckpoint(ctx)`.
    - Creates a commit with the subagent's file changes and metadata including the subagent transcript.

7.  **Cleanup**: Deletes `.entire/tmp/pre-task-<tool-use-id>.json`.

### `PostToolUse[TaskCreate|TaskUpdate]`

- **Command**: `entire hooks claude-code post-todo`
=== line 120-130 ===

5.  **Calculate Token Usage**:

    - Parses the transcript from `StepTranscriptStart` (captured at prompt start) to calculate tokens used in this turn.
    - Extracts token counts from assistant messages: input tokens, cache creation/read tokens, output tokens.
    - Deduplicates by message ID (streaming creates multiple rows per message; uses highest output_tokens).
    - Finds spawned subagents by scanning for `agentId:` in Task tool results.
    - Calculates subagent token usage from their transcript files (`agent-<id>.jsonl`).
    - Aggregates into a `TokenUsage` struct with nested `SubagentTokens`.

6.  **Invoke Strategy**:

    - Builds a `SaveContext` with session ID, file lists, metadata paths, git author info, and token usage.

    - Prefers the current layout: `<transcript_dir>/<session_id>/subagents/agent-<agent_id>.jsonl`
      (Claude Code writes an `agent-<agent_id>.meta.json` sidecar there too, carrying
      `agentType`, `description`, `toolUseId`, and `spawnDepth`).
    - Falls back to the legacy sibling layout `<transcript_dir>/agent-<agent_id>.jsonl`

      Falling back matters: a subagent's Write/Edit calls appear only in its own
      transcript, so a missed subagent transcript means those edits are invisible here
      (they are still picked up at turn end, which is why a wrong path went unnoticed).

git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
fix(subagent): resolve subagent transcripts in Claude Code's current layout

handleLifecycleSubagentEnd looked for the subagent transcript at
<transcriptDir>/agent-<id>.jsonl, a sibling of the main transcript. Claude
Code now nests them: <transcriptDir>/<sessionID>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl
(with an agent-<id>.meta.json sidecar alongside). The old path therefore never
existed, so SubagentTranscriptPath was always empty in production — confirmed
by real logs, where no "subagent completed" line ever carries the
subagent_transcript attribute (it is only logged when the path resolves).

Two consequences: task checkpoints stored no subagent transcript, and file
extraction fell back to scanning the main transcript, where a subagent's
Write/Edit calls never appear. The turn-end extractor already used the correct
nested path, so files were still picked up at Stop — which is what kept the
wrong path unnoticed.

Add ResolveAgentTranscriptPath, which prefers the nested layout and falls back
to the legacy sibling one so older sessions keep working, and route both
call sites through the new SubagentsDir helper.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
